subject.title: [improvement] Sub-agent cascade circuit breaker for multi-agent team reliability

question: Should OpenClaw add a core subagent circuit breaker, and if so should it be opt-in or default-on with conservative thresholds?
rationale: The missing capability is real, but the permanent scope affects config defaults, persisted state, failure classification, session/task semantics, UI/CLI recovery, and overlap with provider and broader session breakers.

options.title: Add opt-in core breaker
options.body: Implement a core opt-in breaker for native and ACP subagent spawn keyed by agent/task signature, with persisted state, structured parent feedback, and explicit status/reset surfaces.

options.title: Fold into session breaker design
options.body: Keep this issue linked but defer implementation until the broader unhealthy-session circuit breaker decides shared state, cooldown, and UI semantics.

options.title: Leave to external hooks
options.body: Close or defer native work and document hook/plugin workarounds for teams that want custom subagent failure policies.

recommendation.title: Add opt-in core breaker
recommendation.body: Implement a core opt-in breaker for native and ACP subagent spawn keyed by agent/task signature, with persisted state, structured parent feedback, and explicit status/reset surfaces.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent subagent spawn, registry, docs, and config-adjacent history makes this the strongest available routing signal for the product/API decision.
